_comment: Every entity key retired by the global free-tier demotion, pinned against the MEASURED retired-key split: ErrNotFound on the exact-key --by-entity seam for all of them, and ErrNotFound on the looser `show` seam too. The split's two ErrAmbiguous rows (bare `ling` and bare `mimo`) are NOT in this set: neither is a key this lever retires, and both remain live family tokens with live children — turning either into a 404 would break three unrelated live-family lookups. `ling/flash-free@2.6` is likewise absent: it SURVIVES the demotion under an exact-ID pin and is asserted live by the companion test. Each case also carries the MEASURED migration record: `retired_instances` is the exact set of provider instances the key held immediately before the lever (spelled `<provider>|<model id>`, read off the pre-lever generated catalog), and `successors` is the set of entity keys those instances now belong to. A successor set is NOT an assumption that a key folds onto its bare parent — two of these keys SPLIT across three successors each, because peeling `free` exposed versions the fused suffix had been hiding. The successor set is re-derived from `retired_instances` against the live registry on every run and compared against this record, and the CHANGELOG migration table is compared against it too, so the three cannot drift apart silently. See TESTING.md.

provenance.ref: the epoch-wide retired-key policy: a retired entity key is a uniform hard 404 on both seams — no alias, no redirect, no successor listing. The CHANGELOG old->new table is the only pointer a user gets.
